definition: A topological sort orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph so every edge points from earlier to later. It is an order in which prerequisite tasks can be done. If the graph has a cycle, no such order exists.
details: Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes a vertex with no incoming edges, using a queue. Depth-first search can emit vertices in reverse order of finishing instead.
Several valid orders may exist when some tasks do not depend on each other.
examples: Ordering build steps so each step runs after the ones it needs
